svg.text: WLD 205 DAY 9 — INSTRUCTOR KEY / DELIVERY GUIDE
Integrated Readiness: Blueprint + Math + Material Behavior
0–10 MIN — QUICK CHECK (Q1–9)
Blueprint Q1–3: units/source, WPS/SWPS source, unclear-symbol STOP/CHECK.
Material Q7–9: ductility; HAZ; exact alloy from documentation/marking/MTR/spec.
Use results to assign ONE mini-station. Do not rank students or repeat strong domains.
10–25 MIN — TARGETED REPAIR MINI-STATION
Blueprint Locate: use Bridge Print C; units, material note, two layout dimensions, procedure source.
Material Behavior: hardness ≠ toughness; HAZ = heated/unmelted base metal; exact grade is source-controlled.
Model one clean correction only. Then reduce prompting and require independent evidence.
25–48 MIN — BRIDGE PRINT C / BASE-C (Q10–14)
Q10: overall plate = 10.000 × 6.000 in.
Q11: centered on 10.000-in length = nominal center 5.000 in.
Q13: “carbon steel” does not establish exact carbon content/grade; use source documentation.
Q14: HAZ is the zone beside the weld that may have changed properties.
Require the worksheet chain: READ → CALCULATE → CHECK SOURCE → DECIDE → DOCUMENT.
48–56 MIN — PARALLEL RECHECK
Select one NEW item only in the weakest remaining domain.
Blueprint: B1–B3. Math/Tolerance: M1–M3. Material Behavior: R1–R3.
A clean independent response closes the gap for today. Do not drill a secure domain.
If still weak, record the specific support item and carry only that gap forward.
56–60 MIN — READINESS CLOSE
Record one demonstrated Level I strength, one remaining support item, and the evidence.
Day 10 = WLD-210 overlap. Day 11 begins common WLD-205 sequence. This is readiness evidence, not credential evidence.
Instructor rule: CHECK → IDENTIFY GAP → REPAIR ONE DOMAIN → INTEGRATE → RECHECK → RECORD
